thread:
maya: Quick Q — around model/version pinning and deprecation comms. PR #4321 tweaks the header handling for model pins and I want to align on: should server change default model variants (i.e., flip what unpinned calls resolve to) be treated as a breaking change we never do without a deprecation window? If so, what timeframe (60/90/180 days)? Also, do we expect clients to opt into pinning via a header/query param, or should we enforce server-side pins for older API versions?

alex: Short answer: changing what an unpinned request resolves to is breaking for app behavior. We should avoid silent flips. Recommended: keep resolution stable for a deprecation window and provide an explicit header for clients to override. Server-side recommended policy: 1) explicit header/query param for pinning, 2) server default can change only after deprecation.

jonathan: Example header/param proposal (from PR #4321):
```
# header approach
X-Redwood-Model: redwood-alpha-v2

# query param approach (fallback)
?model=redwood-alpha-v2&model_pin=true
```
If model_pin=true, runtime must return 409 if requested model unavailable? Or fallback to nearest compatible model? Need to decide fallback semantics.

rob: For rollouts — we should treat default-resolution flips like any other breaking API change: announce, console banner, SDK deprecation warnings, and a migration guide. Timeline suggestion: minor behavior tweaks (non-deterministic quality changes) = 60 days, default-model flips = 90 days, hard removals/major breaking (remove header) = 180 days.

tara: SDK side: we can add warnings in SDKs when they call without a pin. For migration doc: include quick diff snippets, e.g., change code from
```
client.generate({ model: 'default' })
```
to
```
client.generate({ model: 'redwood-alpha-v2' })
```
I'll prep a migration doc if we lock timeline. Also +1 to making header the primary surface.

maya: @alex @tara so consensus = header primary, query param as compatibility layer, deprecation windows based on severity (>=90 for default flips). Who will own the public comms + console banner?

alex: I'll own the banner and the console messaging. I'll add a checkbox in the rollout playbook: GH issue, console banner, SDK warnings, customer email for orgs with high usage.

jonathan: Fallback semantics — prefer explicit fallback policy: default behavior for unpinned when requested model missing: 1) if request included model_pin=true or X-Redwood-Model -> return 404/409 and surface an error to force explicit migration; 2) if unpinned -> use server compatibility routing and log an event for customers hit by a change. That keeps breaking behavior opt-in.

rob: +1. Also note we need metric hooks: count of unpinned calls, % using header, and regressions post-change. I'll add telemetry tasks to the rollouts card.

infra-bot: deploy: model-router v1.3.4 scheduled to canary at 2026-06-03 02:00 UTC (tracking: infra/2238).

sre-oncall: We'll add alerts for spike in errors or latency during rollout window and a runbook link. If we see >1% error increase for 15min we'll rollback.

maya: OK — plan from this thread:
- alex: console banner + comms (EPIC: PLAT-985)
- jonathan: final header/param spec + fallback semantics PR (assign: #4321)
- tara: migration doc + SDK warnings PR
- rob: telemetry and rollout checklist
- maya: put schedule on eng calendar and notify customer-facing teams

I'll open a tracking issue combining these bits. Thanks all :thumbsup:
